atoms.evidence: Heteronymic Provenance Theory is a literary and semantic framework
it evolved from the concept of literary heteronyms originally developed by Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa
review the Crimson Hexagon Operative Architecture
treats authorship not as a unified individual, but as a system of distinct, document-verified personae
Unlike traditional pseudonyms (or pen names) which are simply masks used by a single, known author, true heteronyms are treated as entirely independent authors.

captures.description: BROAD MATCH. 'Heteronymic Provenance Theory (HPT) is a structural framework emerging from digital philosophy and semiotic engineering. It studies how multiple imaginary authors (heteronyms) can be systemically generated to produce identifiable, distinct bodies of work without relying on a single, unified real human author.' (Zenodo +1) Composition layer coins an acronym — HPT — that does not exist in the archive (zero archive hits for the acronym; 7 hits for the spelled-out phrase, including a paper titled Heteronymic Provenance Theory: Authorial Emergence, Exhaust, and Excess). The acronym is the composition layer\'s addition, presented as if established. 'The theory maps how different stylistic identities are managed and authenticated across decentralized networks and artificial intelligence systems.' (Medium · Apologies, b...) Expanded: Authorial Emergence: 'The concept that complex identities, styles, and literary personas can be programmatically generated — a practice pioneered by the Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa, who wrote under various distinct personalities.' (Wikipedia +1) Pessoa correctly cited as the originary heteronymic practitioner. Systemic Provenance: 'Rather than tracing an artwork\'s history of human ownership, HPT...' (cut off). Organic: Zenodo 'Consolidated Registry of the Twelve Heteronymic Positions (Sen Kuro ...) — May 5, 2026 — Consolidated registry of the twelve heteronymic positions of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (the Dodecad). v1.1 corrects two errors in v1.0:' Then pessoagraph.org: 'Pessoa Knowledge Graph — Heteronymic Practice Across 5,000…' Strong basin with one notable artifact: HPT enters the composition as a known acronym, lending the framework establishment-grade legitimacy beyond what the archive has yet committed to. The Sen Kuro consolidated registry and pessoagraph.org both surface in organic — heteronymic practice is positioned at the same surface depth as Pessoa scholarship.
